newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL plunge not good for APV - director.
newsitem.headline: MOL plunge not good for APV - director.

text.p: Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt said a recent sharp fall in oil and gas company MOL Rt share prices was not beneficial ahead of the second phase of MOL's privatisation.
"This is not good for us," APV's general director Pal Szabo told a news conference on Wednesday.
APV said on January it would continue MOL's privatisation but gave no details.
The price of the shares to be sold has not been decided yet, but the bourse price of the stocks is believed to influence the privatisation price.
APV holds a 58 percent stake in MOL, which has issued share capital of 98.4 billion forints and the privatisation law says APV has to retain a 25 percent plus one share stake in the company.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, MOL shares closed at 3,115 forints, up 105, after a peak of 3,790 forints on February 5.
